speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I see you've had a tympanoplasty and are experiencing shooting ear pain with difficulty wearing earrings. How many days ago was your surgery performed?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the detailed history; the timing of the pain relative to eating suggests possible myringitis or a neuroma, but I need to assess the ear canal directly. Can you tell me if the shooting pain is accompanied by any discharge, fever, or a feeling of fullness in the right ear? Also, does the pain radiate specifically to the jaw or temple when you chew?

REQUEST IMAGES: Otoscopy_Right_Ear

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigeminal Neuralgia (specifically involving the V3 distribution, likely due to post-surgical irritation or compression)

Based on your description of shooting pain triggered specifically by chewing and the lack of infectious signs, I need to confirm if the pain is strictly unilateral and if any touch to the ear canal or jaw triggers it. Can you confirm if touching the area causes the same electric shock sensation?
